subject: Re: Northbridge AI — evaluation & onramp: model recommendations and benchmark plan
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.dev>
To: Samir Patel <samir@northbridge.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.dev>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.dev>
Date: Tue, Apr 6, 2027 at 2:05 PM -0700
Subject: Northbridge eval kickstart — recommended models, dataset format, and next steps

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can kick off a focused evaluation on Redwood.

Key takeaways from our discovery:
- Primary use case: document summarization + extractive QA for internal compliance and customer support triage.
- Scale: ~1M docs ingested/year, peak request latency requirement 350ms P95, retention policy 90 days.
- Sensitive content: PII present in ~12% of docs — security questionnaire in flight.

Model recommendations (initial shortlist for the pilot):
1) redwood-2-medium (float16) — baseline for quality/latency tradeoff
2) red-llama-13b-q4_0 — cost-optimized candidate with fast token throughput
3) redwood-2-small-quant (8-bit) — fallback for high-concurrency routing

Why these: we expect redwood-2-medium to give the best quality out of box for summarization and long-context prompts, while the quantized Llama variant provides a cost baseline to estimate unit economics. We recommend running A/B comparisons on the same prompt bank and measuring quality/cost/latency jointly.

Eval plan summary (what we need from Northbridge):
- Sample dataset: 500–1,000 representative items to start. CSV format preferred with columns: id, prompt, context, expected_response, category, severity. (See attached "northbridge_prompt_samples.csv" for a small sample and "northbridge_benchmark_template.yaml" for the scorer config.)
- Scoring criteria: primary metric = ROUGE-L / F1 on extraction tasks; secondary = hallucination rate (binary judge), safety flags rate, and latency at P95. Pass threshold for pilot: ROUGE-L >= 0.48 and hallucination <= 4%.
- Human scorer instructions: blind scoring, at least two independent annotators per item; calculate inter-annotator agreement and surface disagreements.

Operational items Redwood will run for the pilot:
- Provision sandbox endpoints (dedicated, isolated project) with model variants pinned.
- Run 3x A/B runs: redwood-2-medium vs red-llama-13b-q4_0 vs redwood-2-small-quant.
- Collect token-level cost, per-request latency, and model output artifacts.

Next steps / ask from you by EOD Thu:
- Share the 500–1,000 sample rows (or a redacted subset) in the Drive link I shared.
- Confirm the scoring team (name + email) and whether we can use Redwood's scorer UI or your internal annotators.
- Preferred time for a two-hour kickoff with engineering + security next week.

Attachments: northbridge_prompt_samples.csv, northbridge_benchmark_template.yaml

Thanks — I’ll loop Ben (SE) on the technical checklist and Jordan on rollout/contract items.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.dev

Subject: RE: Northbridge eval kickstart — sandbox isolation notes and economics

Hi Samir — Ben from Redwood inference here. Short answers below: 

Sandbox isolation (pilot):
- We create a dedicated Redwood project with isolated compute that does not share persistent KV caches with other customers. Data stays on the provisioned project and is deleted per the agreed retention window (90 days). We can enable customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest on request. Audit logs for all API calls are available and we’ll share a temp report for the pilot window.

Cost delta (very rough):
- redwood-2-medium (float16): ~ $12 / 1k input+output tokens for pilot throughput baseline
- red-llama-13b-q4_0 (quantized): ~ $4.50 / 1k tokens (estimating 2.6-2.7x cost savings vs medium)
- redwood-2-small-quant: ~ $2.8 / 1k tokens (fast, lower-quality fallback)

Notes on evaluation & regression concerns:
- Keep the prompt bank frozen during the A/B runs to avoid data drift.
- We recommend an automated regression check: if F1 drops >8% vs baseline on control prompts, we flag and pause rollout.
- For hallucination detection, run both automated heuristics (precision on entity overlap) and human adjudication for edge cases.

I’ll attach a short sandbox runbook and the cost assumptions spreadsheet to the Drive folder.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
